images.prompt: Key art for an original family fantasy campaign called The Lighthouse Between Winds (DO NOT render any title). A vast archipelago of floating rocky islands above an ocean of luminous dusk clouds. A graceful stone lighthouse rises from a distant island, four immense brass orbital rings around its glass lantern dome. In the foreground, a small seaworthy flying timber houseboat with a copper roof and chimney, one cream sail with a teal patch, one round amber lantern; its warm lit windows promise a home. The ship sails from lower left toward the lighthouse in the upper right, wondrous bridges, tiny waterfalls and stars receding into mist. Big beautiful readable silhouettes and inviting detail. No people in close-up. A compelling cinematic cover with breathing room in the upper left.

A playable establishing scene: the floating island town Lantern Harbor on festival evening, seen at street level across a broad cobbled plaza. Warm crooked timber houses, copper roofs, fabric awnings, suspended amber lanterns, a tiny pastry stall, a public fountain, arched gate to a distant airship dock. Beyond the quay an ocean of pink and blue clouds and floating islands. A few small friendly adult townsfolk at the edges; unobstructed center for players to imagine standing in the scene. A little flying houseboat at the dock has a copper roof, chimney, one cream sail with teal patch and round amber lantern. The town feels inhabited, not a theme park. No secret symbols or puzzle solutions.

Interior of a tiny flying houseboat: a warmly lit timber cabin with a large oval window overlooking a vast cloud sea, a brass kettle steaming on a compact stove, three mismatched chairs around a round map table, folded teal blankets, drawers for travel treasures and a hammock. A small brass mechanical fox with turquoise glass eyes, one copper ear and an articulated tail sits beside a basket. No visible readable map text. The room is a real cozy home between adventures; composition creates a welcoming playable scene.

A spectacular floating orchard island at golden morning, ancient apple trees with spiralling copper wind chimes and luminous amber fruit, little rope bridges linking mossy terraces above clouds. A vast friendly tortoise with a garden growing on its shell sleeps beside a broken water wheel. Elegant glass irrigation channels and a broad grassy clearing with a picnic cloth. Wondrous scale, no peril, no people in foreground.

The Library of Tides, a magnificent circular hall cut into a floating pearl-white rock. Curving bookcases and brass ladders surround a shallow mirror-like pool that reflects stars in daytime. Small paper boats carry books along narrow turquoise channels. Arched windows look onto drifting clouds; warm reading lamps and a broad accessible walkway. A huge gentle sky whale visible far beyond one window. Books have no readable letters. Dreamlike but credible architecture.

The Mirror Bazaar at blue hour, a playful sophisticated open air market built on interlocking floating stone terraces. Tall freestanding mirrors in ornate copper frames reflect harmless alternate seasonal scenery, stalls sell bottled breezes, folded kites and ribbon spools. Indigo canvas roofs, strings of soft amber lamps, mosaic paving, distant cloud sea. Elegant clear central path, no sinister faces, no puzzle codes, only tiny adult background silhouettes.

The Cloud Forge, a spectacular open-air brass and stone workshop built inside the curved hollow of a floating basalt island. Immense copper wind wheels, suspended silk sails, brilliant turquoise harmless plasma in a contained furnace, amber work lamps, tool benches and broad safe stone bridges with railings. Clouds stream through the background arches. No people foreground. Breathtaking industrial fantasy craftsmanship with a coherent sense of scale.

The Observatory on the Back of a Sky Whale. A vast serene cobalt whale floats through a starry dusk ocean of clouds, its curved back supporting a small white observatory with brass telescope and warm windows, a wooden landing jetty and a hanging garden. Seen from a nearby low flight angle so the observatory and the whale's gentle eye are both readable. Tiny cream-sailed timber houseboat approaching in the distance. Magical natural majesty, completely peaceful and safe.

The City of Listening Bells: a sunlit floating island city with tall slender copper bell towers, bridges between tiled roofs, hundreds of little hanging bells and ribbons stirring in gentle wind. A broad circular plaza surrounds four differently shaped big bells on a low wooden stage. Misty pink morning clouds below, warm ochre plaster and teal patina, no writing and no visual solution code. Lived-in, witty details, sophisticated painted fantasy.

The Palace of the Still Minute, a poignant quiet winter glass conservatory on a floating island, viewed from inside a tall arched entrance. Frost flowers on huge glass panes, a marble floor, one suspended golden leaf frozen halfway to the floor, a tea table set for two adults, enormous brass clockwork with no visible numbers. Cold blue silver light balanced by a single warm amber desk lamp, wistful but not frightening. No people, no ghost or death imagery.

The great Lighthouse Between Winds at the campaign climax, a beautiful stone tower on a small floating island over an indigo cloud sea. Four huge brass rings surround its glass lantern dome. A broad stone arrival bridge with solid railings leads into an open circular machinery court, four approachable copper control podiums surround an empty central platform. Storm clouds in the far distance with a warm dawn break, dramatic hope, no characters, no disaster or violence. No text, no puzzle answers.
images.editPrompt: Edit target: the attached lighthouse environment painting. Preserve the entire beautiful composition, stone tower, glass lantern dome, sunset, colors, brushwork, floating island, entry bridge, all four control desks and the atmosphere. One precise correction: the story requires EXACTLY FOUR distinct large brass orbital rings encircling the glass lantern dome, but the target visibly has only three. Add a fourth complete brass ring, elegantly spaced so that all FOUR rings are easy to count, with four separate circular mounting joints down the vertical left support. Keep their believable perspective and physical construction. Slightly enlarge the space occupied by the rings if needed without covering the dome. Do not change the number of control desks (four). No text, no symbols, no people, no added features elsewhere. Final landscape aspect ratio 3:2, same premium gouache fantasy environment art and resolution.
